newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end quietly higher, focus on budget.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end quietly higher, focus on budget.

text.p: 1620 GMT - UK gilts closed quietly higher in line with Treasuries after a slow day as Q3 GDP data and Q2 c/a data came in in line with market expectations. Buying interest was muted ahead of next Tuesday's budget.
* Dec long gilt contract settled 14/32 higher at 110-22/32

"Overall these figures paint a fairly rosy picture of the UK economy. GDP growth is a little way above its trend, consumer spending growth is fast but not yet unsustainable and the current account position is healthy," said Andrew Cates, economist at UBS.
However, some economists were concerned about the strong pickup in consumer spending and the implications this could have for inflation and interest rates.
"The rise in nominal spending supports the Bank of England's view that base rates need to rise further to keep inflation low further out," said Michael Saunders of Salomon Brothers.
Cates said the GDP deflator showed inflationary pressures were starting to build.
"The economy needs a marked expansion in capital spending to ensure that increased consumer demand does not leak into imports or into even higher prices," he said.

March short sterling closed up one basis point at 93.26, implying a 75-basis point rise in official interest rates from the present 6.0 percent by the end of the first quarter. The 10-year gilt/Bund spread narrowed to 179 basis points from 184 on Wednesday.
The Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged at its regular council and markets expect no change in German interest rates before the year-end.
Adams said gilts should remain quiet ahead of the budget, which markets generally expect to be cautious.
A Reuters poll of 27 London-based economists suggested Chancellor Kenneth Clarke will give away a modest 2.25 billion stg in net tax cuts.
